text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The military claims in a document presented to the constitutional court that former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party received money from Libya.
MILLIYET
- The chances of establishing peace in the divided island of Cyprus are remote as two parties are still suspicious of each other.
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz warns German Chancellor Helmut Kohl over the phone about the European Union decision to give Greek Cyprus membership of the EU.
HURRIYET
- Leftist opposition leader Deniz Baykal says the recent price in petroluem products is ruthless.
- The new anti-Islamist government is preparing a draft law that will give civil servants the right to be unionised.
YENI YUZYIL
- The armed forces asks for legal action against previous interior minister Meral Aksener for insulting the military.
- Trade union Hak-Is declares monthly food expenses of a famly of four as 33 million lira.
RADIKAL
- Parliament's summer holiday will begin in August 1.
- Turkish lira weakened against the dollar by 1,150 lira in a day.
CUMHURIYET
- Education ministry asks to employ 25,000 teachers to implement eight-year compulsory education plan.
- An Islamist deputy resigns from his party.
DUNYA
- The new government's price for cotton is awaited to see if it keeps up with the high prices given to agricultural products by the previous Islamist-led government.
ZAMAN
- Ankara's recent decision to increase its opium poppy plantation was taken because the United Nations asked for it.
